limitations: Private agreements and redacted terms limit verification.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic depend on billions in big tech cloud credits to run their very expensive models.

statement.excerpt: The two most prevalent Large Language Models (outside Meta’s Llama) — OpenAI’s GPT and Anthropic’s Claude — are effectively big tech’s welfare recipients, receiving billions in cloud credits to run their extremely-expensive models without having to build out their own infrastructure.

from_speaker: without having to build out their own infrastructure
our_interpretation: The assessed proposition is dependence on large technology companies' cloud support; welfare recipients is rhetorical.
Cloud credits means rights to consume cloud services supplied as funding or support. Cash investment, cloud purchasing obligations and discounts are distinct unless their equivalence is established.
The wording may mean billions collectively or billions for each company. Both readings require actual amounts attributable to cloud credits.
The observation concerns funding and computing arrangements operating during 2024 through the post date, not credits newly issued only during that interval.
The claim gives no accounting basis for the cloud-credit amount. It is therefore unknown.
The prevalence aside has no named usage measure and is not treated as a precise market-share ranking.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable terms quantify billions of dollars of cloud credits supplied to the named labs and establish material reliance on the providers' infrastructure to train or run their models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Complete comparable terms establish materially less than billions in cloud credits, or establish that the labs did not materially depend on those providers' infrastructure.
